edges.description: Reads out residual human pyridoxal kinase activity by complementation: an allele that fails to rescue the fly phenotype has lost function.
edges.limitations: Two limitations matter and neither is small. The readouts are chromosome aberrations and haemolymph glucose, not neuropathy, so the system reports on enzyme competence rather than on disease mechanism. And the four human alleles actually tested in this study (D87H, V128I, H246Q, A243G) are population variants and a gestational-diabetes variant, NOT the p.Ala228Thr, p.Arg220Gln, p.Asn75Lys or p.Thr148Met alleles that cause this disease. The model therefore establishes that the assay works and that reduced-activity PDXK alleles exist in the population; it says nothing directly about the disease alleles.

edges.limitations: Dietary deprivation in a wild-type animal is not the human lesion, which is a constitutive enzyme defect with normal dietary intake. nodes.description: Pyridoxal kinase phosphorylates the dietary B6 vitamers pyridoxal, pyridoxine and pyridoxamine, and is the rate-limiting step of the vitamin B6 salvage pathway in humans, who cannot synthesize the vitamin de novo. Two routes to reduced catalysis are documented. In the missense alleles the protein is made in normal amounts but its catalytic pocket is misshapen: circular dichroism showed rearranged aromatic side-chains around the pocket, isothermal titration calorimetry showed the p.Ala228Thr mutant no longer binds ATP, and kinetics showed a roughly doubled Km for pyridoxal together with a fall in Vmax. In the more recently described splice-altering allele the enzyme is not misfolded at all; the transcript is aberrantly spliced and degraded, so less enzyme is made.

nodes.description: PLP is the cofactor for well over a hundred enzymes covering amino-acid, lipid and carbohydrate metabolism, neurotransmitter synthesis and catabolism, and one-carbon metabolism, and it also acts as an antioxidant. Which of those dependencies actually fails first in a neuron is not established, and this node is deliberately marked provisional for that reason. The leading candidate is GABA synthesis, because glutamate decarboxylase is PLP-dependent and because compounds that inhibit pyridoxal kinase cause convulsions and lower GABA; the proposed consequence is excitotoxic injury to sensory neurons. The founding study was explicit that it could not fully explain the mechanism linking low PLP to the clinical picture.

nodes.description: The disease-directed treatment, and the reason this entity matters disproportionately to its rarity. The logic is kinetic rather than a simple bypass: the mutant enzyme has roughly twice the normal Km for pyridoxal, so giving oral PLP, which is hydrolysed to pyridoxal before cellular uptake, raises the substrate concentration the residual enzyme sees and forces flux through it. Fifty milligrams a day was enough to bring plasma PLP above the normal range within two weeks. Over 18 to 24 months the treated siblings gained 8 and 6 points on the MRC sum score, regained independent walking, reported less pain and fatigue, showed no further electrophysiological progression, and had plasma neurofilament light chain fall to the normal range. Sensory examination and vision did not improve, so this is arrested and partially reversed motor decline rather than cure, and the evidence is an uncontrolled observation in two patients.

nodes.description: Loss of retinal ganglion cell axons produces optic atrophy on fundoscopy with reduced visual acuity and colour vision. Its timing is the striking feature: in the founding family it appeared between 29 and 50 years of age, decades after the neuropathy, and in an adolescent with established neuropathy the only finding was mild thinning of the peripapillary retinal nerve fibre layer on optical coherence tomography, with normal visual evoked potentials. Absence of optic atrophy in a young patient therefore does not exclude the diagnosis, and OCT may detect the arm before fundoscopy does.

nodes.description: The biochemical signature of the disease, and the one that makes it treatable and monitorable. Plasma PLP falls while the other B6 vitamers (pyridoxal, pyridoxine, pyridoxamine and the excretion product 4-pyridoxic acid) do not, which is what localizes the block to the kinase step rather than to intake or absorption. Erythrocyte pyridoxal kinase activity measured directly in dried blood spots is correspondingly reduced. The depletion is not invariable: one adolescent had a plasma PLP within the reference range that was nonetheless about 2.5-fold below her parents' levels.

It is the only experimental evidence bearing on the tissue selectivity that makes this a peripheral-nerve disease rather than an encephalopathy: on B6 deprivation, pyridoxal kinase activity falls quickly in liver, muscle and plasma while brain activity and B6 supply are maintained.

The only whole-organism system in which human PDXK has been assayed by complementation. Loss of the fly pyridoxal kinase ortholog produces chromosome aberrations and raised larval haemolymph glucose, and expressing wild-type human PDXK rescues both, which makes the fly a functional assay for whether a given human PDXK allele retains activity.
